quest.title: Natlan! A New Adventure
quest.description: You've made many unforgettable memories in Fontaine. Now, a new journey lies before you — first, time to say goodbye to your fine Fontainian friends.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.title: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, time flies! Just like that, it's time for us to embark on the next phase of our journey!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We need to head to Natlan next.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neuvillette called it "a nation of dragons," but that description doesn't give us much to go off of...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We haven't met anyone from Natlan either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Even when Inazuma was completely closed-off, we still managed to run into people from there in other nations...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, could it be... that there are no humans in Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Yes, yes! That look of surprise and excitement is perfect! Hold it right there... Now, look at the Kamera, and big smiles on three, ready?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! Just make sure to get Paimon's good side!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, hang on a minute... What's with the photo shoot, Charlotte?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Well, I heard you two were about to leave for the next part of your journey. After everything you did for Fontaine, The Steambird simply had to follow up on a scoop like that.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: *sigh* I have a feeling we're going to be short on material once you're gone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you knew we were leaving... We don't need a big send-off. That's not really our thing.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hehe, yeah, that's definitely not your style, but we got to thinking... and, well, a little change never hurt anyone, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "We"?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: All those obstacles we overcame side by side... Feels like it was just yesterday! Don't be a stranger, now, partner!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: If you encounter any troubles along your journey, you need only let us know, no matter the distance between us.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Partings are inevitable, of course, but distance makes the heart grow fonder, right?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: One thing will never change, though. We'll always have the memories we made together during this time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, you're all here!

choices.text: I'm sure we'll meet again.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That we will! I'm looking forward to hearing about your future adventures, so make sure to stop by and tell us about them sometime!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Well, in light of your impending departure, shall we take a photo together?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ooh, great idea! We even have a professional photographer with us. Charlotte, would you do us the honor?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Leave it to me. Just give me a moment to set the Kamera up.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh, by the way, you're overthinking the whole Natlan issue, Paimon. Natlan has human inhabitants and its own unique culture, just like Fontaine.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: It's just that, because of their local customs, the native people choose not to leave.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: They're not unwelcoming to outsiders, though. People travel there for business and leisure alike, and usually return with nothing but good things to say.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Many members of the Spina have visited in the past, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's a relief! Hopefully, we don't get swept up in any major drama this time!

choices.text: Don't speak too soon.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Well, given your experience and skill in that regard, I have no doubt you'll be able to overcome anything that comes your way.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Still, I hope you can avoid danger this time around. An uneventful trip might be a nice change of pace.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Alright, I'm ready! Shall we?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: #Well then, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Bon voyage!

choices.text: Hope you didn't just jinx us.
Let me know the next time a festival rolls around!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Already thinking about taking time off? Any excuse for a party, huh...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But yes, you can count on us! We wouldn't let you miss out on all the fun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! So, this is Natlan!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So many strange mountains! And so many animals Paimon has never seen before!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Huh, doesn't look like there are any cities around here, though. Where should we start?

choices.text: Let's try heading this way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea. Finding people means we can learn information about the local Archon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And once we've met the Archon, we should have a better idea of what to expect during our journey.

choices.text: If experience is anything to go by, that should be the case.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon hopes this one is easy to get along with. As long as we don't get on their bad side, we should be fine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, let's keep following the road.

choices.text: Archons have the deepest connection to their respective nations.
I see signs of human habitation.

dialogues.speaker: Tlaco
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Kachina. I know it's not right for us to go back on our word like this, but Cempoa and I have to do well during this Pilgrimage.

dialogues.speaker: Cempoa
dialogues.text: You can't seem to find other people to join our team, and we don't have time to sit around and wait.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: B—But if you two leave, I'll be the only one left...

dialogues.speaker: Cempoa
dialogues.text: We really are sorry, but you still have plenty of chances... You're young, and you bear an Ancient{RUBY#[D]tocaitl} Name on top of that.

dialogues.speaker: Cempoa
dialogues.text: We're just ordinary tribal warriors with years of battle under our belt, and no glory to show for it. Not to mention the physical toll of all that fighting... We're no longer in our prime.

dialogues.speaker: Tlaco
dialogues.text: We barely had a chance last time, remember? We can't expect a better result with even fewer people.

dialogues.speaker: Tlaco
dialogues.text: Pilgrimage registration closes tonight. This is our last chance to switch teams.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Well, alright. I guess it is what it is...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I just wish I was stronger. I'm nothing compared to the other Ancient Name bearers...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: But never mind — guess this is par for the course as Utha{RUBY#[D]Resilience}biti, huh? I'm sure I'll figure something out.

dialogues.speaker: Tlaco
dialogues.text: Well, if we do well this time, there's still a spot for you at the Victory Feast.

dialogues.speaker: Cempoa
dialogues.text: Yeah! Even though we're not participating in the competition together, we're still friends, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Of course... Anyway, you guys should get going before it's too late. Go form a really strong team, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Guess I'll have to wait until the next Pilgrimage...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like that girl over there was just abandoned... Wonder what happened. Aw, she looks so sad, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go check on her.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh gosh, um... I'm fine! Don't worry about me... Wait, I haven't seen you around the tribe before. Are you travelers?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup! We just got to Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh! Welcome, welcome! I'm Kachina. "Utha{RUBY#[D]Resilience}biti" Kachina.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Uthabiti"...?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, that's something we call an Ancient Name. It's a tradition we have here in Natlan, although it's kind of complicated to explain. You can think of it like a "title" for now.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: If you're here for the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, you'll find out what they mean soon enough!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, this Pilgrimage... Is that what you were discussing earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! It's a competition we hold every so often, where everyone competes to try and get the highest ranking.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The competition receives tons of attention, so if you place highly, you're guaranteed instant acclaim, and you earn the right to take part in the "Night Warden Wars."

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Basically, the winners become heroes! And that's pretty much everyone's goal around here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a massive fighting tournament or something... Do you have to be in a team to participate?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Well, due to the sheer number of participants, the Pilgrimage is actually divided into two phases.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Phase one is a team competition. Usually, an Ancient Name bearer serves as the team captain and leads their team in various battles around Natlan, with the goal of capturing Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, and an Ancient Name bearer is just someone with one of those "titles" I mentioned earlier... someone like me!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Once the team competition is over, the participants from the winning teams qualify to take part in individual, one-on-one matches.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like some kind of Natlan National Games.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, the scale seems pretty huge!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute... If Ancient Name bearers lead the teams... That means you must be a team captain!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Sure am! Although... I don't exactly have any team members anymore, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: "The key to winning is in the strength of the team captain," that's what everyone says. But, uh... the difference in strength between bearers can practically be night and day.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: ...So, their decision does make sense. I'd feel the same way if I were in their shoes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's your plan now?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: All Ancient Name bearers have to take part — it's our duty. So, if no one wants to be on my team, then I'll just go it alone.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: At worst, I'm looking at a few extra scrapes and scratches. I'm not great at fighting, but I always manage to get back on my feet in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Psst, {NICKNAME}! Based on the direction of this conversation, Paimon thinks it might be time for us to do our thing...

choices.text: Right there with you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup yup! Time for the next phase of our journey to start for real!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Um, what are you guys talking about?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can we join your team?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: H—Huhhhh!?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Ah, sorry. Didn't mean to freak out on you, I just, uh... How should I put this...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I really appreciate the offer! That's so, unbelievably generous of you! But, only people from Natlan are allowed to take part in the Pilgrimage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh! Paimon thought we could just join your team, fight our way to the top, and then become heroes...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It's alright! Really! I—I mean... No one's ever offered to join my team before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: We're all usually on good terms, but whenever Pilgrimage registration rolls around, it feels like everyone starts avoiding me.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: They don't make eye contact or bring up the Pilgrimage... It's like they're afraid I'll ask them to join my team.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I probably don't even need to explain the reason... I'm too weak.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It's pretty obvious there's nothing to gain from being on my team. That really doesn't matter to you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh, don't you worry! {NICKNAME}'s strong enough for the three of us. Gods, dragons, giant narwhals... {M#He}{F#She} can give 'em all a run for their Mora!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, I get it! You were able to overlook my lack of strength because you're confident in your own skills!

choices.text: I wasn't thinking about any of that, actually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We always try to help people out during our travels! That's what makes a true adventurer!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: A true adventurer...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: You guys are really special! You know you're strong, but you don't take yourselves too seriously. That's exactly the kind of person I want to become!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: You're planning on staying in Natlan for a little while, right? Mind if I try to learn from you while you're here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Learn from us?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Yeah! You know, like a disciple or a sidekick. You don't even have to teach me anything! I'll just observe!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I promise I won't be in the way! Besides, I can take you to see the sights, and introduce you to Natlan in the meantime!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Seems like she really looks up to you...

choices.text: That's fine with us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Didn't those people from earlier say the registration period was about to end? You don't need to focus on finding new teammates?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Don't worry about it. I wouldn't be able to manage it this close to the deadline, anyway.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I lose all the time. I'm used to it, everyone around me is used to it... So, it's fine! No one expects anything out of me.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: But, if I manage to learn a thing or two from you, I might just pull off a win next time!

choices.text: Well, alright...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Ah, thank you! Who would've thought I'd get the chance to meet such impressive adventurers! Hehe, today must be my lucky day!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Well, come with me, you two. I'll show you where I grew up, and introduce you to our tribe, the Children of Echoes.

choices.text: Don't set your expectations too high. We're just ordinary people.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, of course! Of course! I'm just glad you agreed!

choices.text: But, what about your competition?
You were in a tough spot, and I wanted to help.
Looks like it's that time already.

talks.objective: Follow Kachina to the Children of Echoes

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I got so carried away just now, I didn't consider what would happen if our destinations were different...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Luckily, that's not the case, or... Well, I guess we'd just have to meet up after the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure it's okay you didn't tell the chief about your team?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: *sigh* Chief Pacal's a really nice guy. If he knew the truth, he might even ask to join me.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: But, he's not as young as he used to be, and he's got some old injuries that still bother him. He's not cut out for any more attempts.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: He'll find out what really happened when he sees me compete. I'm sure I'll get an earful for lying... But this is for the best.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're a very considerate person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Your teammates left you high and dry, and you made sure they didn't feel guilty about it!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: It's not their fault! Really! The Pilgrimage is extremely important to the people of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: We all grow up listening to stories about the heroes of the past, and dream of becoming warriors with the strength to defend our nation.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Not out of a selfish desire for glory, but to lend our strength to a greater cause.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Anyway, don't worry about it for now. Once you witness the spectacle for yourself, maybe it'll all start to make more sense!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: It'll also be a great opportunity to experience our culture and history!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Alright, time to leave our settlement. Let's head that way. Our last stop — the Statue of The Seven — is also in that direction. Let's go!

talks.objective: Continue exploring the Children of Echoes' territory

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: This is the most cherished and most sacred item in our tribe. It symbolizes the Wayob that protects us and grants us blessings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Wayob"? Is that a god of some sort?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Sort of... We believe the Wayob dwell beneath the earth, while the Pyro Archon hails from above.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: We hold regular gatherings here, actually. Our chief recounts and interprets dreams relating to our Wayob to decipher its will.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The Wayob know the past and can foresee the future. Isn't that extraordinary?

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Huh? Kachina? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Chief! Oh, let me introduce you. This is Pacal, the chief of our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Chief, these two just arrived in Natlan. They're super accomplished adventurers, and they're letting me stick by them so I can learn a thing or two!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, h—hello...

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Kachina is a child of our tribe. Her safety is my responsibility. So, I'll just come out and say it...

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: I don't know how you met her, but I'm going to need you to prove your identity.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Whoa whoa whoa whoa! There's no need for that, Chief! They're good people! I can feel it!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: A "feeling" isn't going to satisfy your parents, Kachina.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a valid concern. I get it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How about... we show you our Adventurer Handbook? It's where all our previous travels are recorded.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Hmm... The people who belong to the Adventurers' Guild are kind of a mixed bag. I'd prefer something more reliable...

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm... Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: #You're {NICKNAME}! And you're Paimon, {M#his}{F#her} familiar!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon is a guide! Geez, these rumors are getting out of control... Well, okay, maybe this one's not that bad. It does make you seem super powerful and mysterious, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Wait, is there something special about those names?

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: You haven't heard?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Nope.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: #Learn well from {M#him}{F#her}, Kachina. It's unlikely you've ever had a teacher of greater merit.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Really? To earn that kind of praise from the chief... You guys must be even stronger than I thought!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Apologies for not trusting your word.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry about it. You were just doing your duty!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Well, Kachina's still young, so you can never be too careful.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: As for you, Kachina... Isn't registration about to close? Why haven't you headed out yet?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Chief. I told my teammates to go ahead. I'll catch up with them in a bit!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I may not be much of a fighter, but I am quick on my feet, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kachina's trying not to worry him, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: I see... Well, I hope I wasn't interrupting anything just now. If I did, just tell me where you left off, and I might be able to help with the explanations.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Lemme think... I told them about the Wayob, so now's the perfect time to dive into Ancient Names! Good thing you're here, Chief. I don't think I could explain it very well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! That word kept popping up in our conversation earlier. So, what does it mean, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Well, Natlan is a nation of heroes, whose valiant deeds are preserved and passed down over time in the form of stories.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: You can think of an Ancient Name almost like a label for these stories. By mentioning an Ancient Name, we remind ourselves of the epic sagas of heroes past.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: For example, the most famous bearer of my Ancient Name fought in twenty-seven Night Warden Wars.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: By the time he fought in his last one, he was already over sixty years old.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Even though he wasn't quite where he used to be, physically speaking, he still managed to achieve top rankings during the Pilgrimage! Impressive, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, why do people inherit Ancient Names?

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Ancient Names allow us to preserve the stories of the past. But, they're also much more than that. Think of an Ancient Name almost like an heirloom passed down from generation to generation.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Do you have your stone on you, Kachina?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Of course! Here, take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that black stone looks so mysterious! It's like there's something shiny inside it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It looks like a feather...

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: The Wayob decide who is deserving of inheriting an Ancient Name. Once a successor is selected, the Name becomes theirs to bear, and their deeds are then preserved within it.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: As time passes, Ancient Names come to represent the heroic deeds of more and more bearers, and their value becomes even more profound.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: In turn, the accomplishments preserved within it serve as an inspiration for the next generation of successors.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Just like me, hehe! I'm still not sure why our Wayob chose me, of all people...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: But, if I didn't know the stories of all the past heroes — how they never stopped fighting — I probably would've given up a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So it's like a form of mental fortitude?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Then, you're saying this stone doesn't have any actual power? Like, it's not gonna make Paimon super strong or smart?

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: None at all, and that is precisely how it exercises its unique value.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Think of it this way... If you become a hero because the heavens granted you strength, are your triumphs earned or given?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it. If people start to ask those kinds of questions, the stories suddenly become a lot less inspirational.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Someone had this to say about Ancient Names:

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: "Our forebearers carved 'miracles' into obsidian rock, yet future bearers looked upon them and saw 'strength.'"

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: The miracles of the past become the motivations of the present. The limitations of the past become the breakthroughs of today... That's more or less the gist of it.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: So, there's no rush, Kachina. Many people struggle to understand the Wayob's judgment after receiving an Ancient Name.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: As long as you never stop trying to improve your abilities and surpass yourself, your time will come.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Thank you, Chief! I'll get it together, just you watch!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Well, it's getting late. I've gotta get to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Ah, right! I'm not sure where you're headed, but... Mind taking a detour with me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that where the Pilgrimage is taking place?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yup! And outside of competition season, it's the place where our inter-tribal gatherings are held.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will the Pyro Archon be there?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Of course. She's the most important figure in the entire event!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a plan, then. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: #Well, if {NICKNAME} and Paimon are with you, then I don't need to worry about your safety... Be on your way, now.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Alright, we're off! See you later, Chief!

talks.objective: Continue exploring the Children of Echoes' territory

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Wrooh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, hehe! You're here too, {REALNAME[ID(2)|HOSTONLY(true)]}!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: No way! You have a Saurian companion too! Aww, what a sweet little thing! I think your friend here will get along with Ayo just fine!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Alright, you two go have fun. I've got some important business to handle, and then I'll be right back.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: No mischief, okay? And you'd better not go leading your new friend astray, or I'm telling your parents.

talks.objective: Continue exploring the Children of Echoes' territory
Go to the Statue of The Seven

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, since we're here, you might as well go get your shiny new elemental powers, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's true.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh? You can get elemental power from the Statue of The Seven?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just you watch, Kachina!

talks.objective: Light the Statue of The Seven

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: We've come a long way. How does a break sound?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great idea! All this sightseeing is making Paimon hungry!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You say that as if you use your stomach to see...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, are you all out of candy? I've got some more, if you want. I've also got bread, drinks, fried rice, roasted apples...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! You're practically a walking cafeteria!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I just like bringing a lot of stuff with me. As my mom always says, "it pays to be prepared."

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: They only come in handy every so often, hehe... But, hey! Better late than never, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh? Is everything okay, Traveler? Seems like you've got something on your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just thinking about what happened with the Statue of The Seven.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that was so weird. It has to mean something, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Actually, you know what? It could be because our Archon is different from the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Different how?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Well, I heard that other nations' Archons live a long time and belong to a class of extremely powerful beings known as "gods."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that's not the case in Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Not at all! Every Pyro Archon in Natlan was an ordinary person before taking on the role.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? A human becoming an Archon? Is that even possible?

choices.text: A human ascending to the divine throne...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You find it hard to believe too, huh?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: So that's not normal, then? I guess I've just gotten used to how things are here in Natlan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, based on what we've seen, that's not usually how it works. It can't be that easy for a human to become an Archon, right...?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Pretty sure the Pyro Archon's the only one who can answer that.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I do know this, though — even after becoming the Pyro Archon, the person in the position still grows old and requires rest.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: The Statue of The Seven may look a lot like our current Archon, but that has to be a coincidence... Countless people have held that title over the years.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, I should also mention... The Pilgrimage is actually how we select the Pyro Archon. Anyone can claim the title. You just have to prove your strength!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, the contest is all about how strong you are?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: That's right. We believe performance in battle is the most comprehensive test for a future Archon. Plus, when someone emerges victorious, it's hard to argue with the results.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Our current Archon achieved an overwhelming victory. The result was obvious from the beginning.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Don't just take my word for it, though. Even the tribe elders said they'd never seen an Archon with such strength before.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: But it's just as Chief Pacal said: Today's limits are tomorrow's breakthroughs! Our future Archons will go from strength to strength.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon's gonna ignore the whole "human becoming an Archon" thing for now. It's just... If she's really that strong, do you think that's a good thing or a bad thing for us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we think back to what happened in Inazuma...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd say it depends on how she feels about us.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I wouldn't worry about it, hehe. Our Archon's a wonderful person, and very welcoming to guests. I think you'll get along great!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right! It's not like we're planning on causing trouble either...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It'll all work out! You'll meet her soon enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, Paimon's just about ready to... Huh? What's that?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, we call this a Phlogiston Chiselith. Good things happen if you infuse it with phlogiston.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Lemme give it a try.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Uh, sorry to disappoint, but only people from Natlan can use that power—

choices.text: (That's kind of like what Furina did, but...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, Kachina. We got your hopes up for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: No, no, it's alright. If anything, I'm even more curious now! Were you really able to gain elemental powers just by touching the Statue of The Seven?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: That's something only Vision bearers can use!

choices.text: Yup. It's always been that way.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: C—Could you show me? Only if you want to, I mean... No pressure!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Take it away, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Wow, different elemental powers... wielded by a single person! I've never even heard of something like that!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Let me give it a try!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: ...Nope. Still just Geo.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Anyway, I was right! You really are something special!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just wait until you hear about our previous adventures!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! What's that?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, that's a Qucusaur! They fly high and fast, and they're always full of energy.

choices.text: Reminds me of our time in Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? It's been ages since that day we first saw Dvalin. We've come so far!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, before I forget... We've got a pretty long trek ahead of us, so, here, take this.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: They look like shiny little gems, don't they? Don't be fooled, though, hehe... It's actually candy! My mom made them.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I always bring a few when I know I'm gonna be out and about for a while. A little boost of sugar can really come in handy in a pinch!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon loves candy. Thanks!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's very generous of you!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: My pleasure! My pleasure! I've got all sorts of bits and bobs on me. I'm sure they'll come in handy at some point!

choices.text: "There's something huge, in the sky!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon already made the connection, {NICKNAME}. You don't have to imitate her!

choices.text: Still not too clear on the how or the why, though.

talks.objective: Go to the Statue of The Seven
Go to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The statue is so pretty! Is that what the Pyro Archon is like?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: You betcha! Beautiful, effortlessly confident, and absolutely awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The higher the vantage point, the better the view!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you and Toto close, Kachina?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yup! When I was little, my parents and I went to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to buy a bunch of different fruits, but the cart we were using to transport them flipped over on our way back.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Toto wasn't even half his current size back then, but I still burst into tears when I saw him approach. I was afraid he was going to eat all the Berries and Sunsettias, and leave none left for me.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: In the end, though, he didn't eat a single one, and even chased off a few other Saurians looking to snatch a few for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: After that, he used his big head to help get our cart right side up again.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I've been bringing him fruit ever since. Oh, and, I was the one that named him "Toto," actually.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: With the sheer amount of food he can eat, he pretty much grew like a weed! Before I knew it, he was already this big!

dialogues.speaker: Toto
dialogues.text: Roar~ ♪

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, look over there! That's our destination — the Stadium of the Sacred Flame!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: You can let us off here, Toto. Thanks for the lift!

dialogues.speaker: Toto
dialogues.text: Roar...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: It's an easy walk from here, so I say we head the rest of the way on foot. It'd be quite the trek for Toto, otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true, especially considering his size. Well, seeya later, Toto!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Alright, why don't you go for a stroll while I handle some important business? Don't worry, I'll keep you company once I'm back!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: No mischief, okay? Or I'm telling your parents.

talks.objective: Continue heading toward the Stadium of the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Phew! We made it!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I'm supposed to meet some friends here, but... Hmm, I don't see them anywhere. Maybe they're not here yet...

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Open your eyes, slowpoke! We've been here this entire time! I've already lost track of how long you've kept us waiting!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Listen here, you. It's not just Kinich and Mualani's time you're wasting, but mine too! MINE!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the heck? That's a strange-looking Saurian... Or wait, is it even a Saurian?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Take it down a notch, alright? You don't even know some of these people.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Just because Kachina's too nice to get mad at you doesn't give you an excuse to be rude to her.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: And what are you gonna do about it? You think you're the boss of— Hey! What do you think you're doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Alright, I've put him in a timeout for now. Sorry about that.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Aw, you didn't have to do that! Ajaw just doesn't have much of a filter, that's all. I don't mind!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Eh, he got what he deserved. Let's just hope the lesson sticks this time!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hehe, Mualani! There you are!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Looks like you made some new friends! And here I was worried you ran into trouble on your way here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello! Paimon's Paimon!

choices.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}, a traveler.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: A traveler, you say? You came at the perfect time! The Pilgrimage is a sight to behold this time of year.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I don't see your teammates with you, Kachina. Where are they?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, uh, they... went to join teams with a better chance at winning.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Huh. So, you're saying you've been ditched. Again.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: *sigh* That might give them an advantage during the team stage, but it all comes down to individual strength sooner or later.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Yeah, well, I couldn't even promise them we would make it through the team stage.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: The outcome of the team stage usually depends on the Ancient Name bearer, after all.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hey, now. There's not a single person here that can promise their team victory. You're putting too much pressure on yourself.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Besides, you're not lacking in strength at all. You just need a bit more confidence.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: You were only three victories short of reaching the Night Warden Wars last time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so... If the "Pilgrimage" is like a national sporting competition, then what are the "Night Warden Wars"?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: The former is a battle of skill. The latter is a real "war."

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: A war against our eternal enemy, the Abyss.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Abyss...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, they're here, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, wait a second... You're saying the prize for winning the Pilgrimage is the chance to go to war!?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: That's not too far off. That's why it's called the "Night Warden Wars."

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: The Pilgrimage chooses the strongest warriors among the tribes, and those warriors fight to repel the Abyss in defense of our homeland.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Their names and deeds are then recorded in epic tales passed down over time. That is the highest honor you can achieve in Natlan.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Isn't it dangerous, though?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Yes, but that's the nature of war. Danger comes with the territory.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Resisting the Abyss is our duty, but we're not alone in this fight. We also have the blessing of our Archon, which allows for our safe return.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It's something we call the Ode of Resurrection — which does exactly what it sounds like, basically!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Resurrect people, you mean?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Yup! So, it's not so scary, really. Our Archon's blessing gives us the courage to keep moving forward!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Let's go register. We don't have much time.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Wait, what about you, Kachina? You're not really planning on competing solo, are you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We really wish we could help, but we're not from here, so it doesn't seem like we can take part...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: There's no threshold to the number of participants. With the sheer number of teams, it's practically guaranteed chaos.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: No matter how strong or experienced the warrior, victory is never assured.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: In a situation like that, it's always better to have someone to watch your back.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Ooh, how about this! When we register, why don't we ask if these two can have special permission to participate?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Odds are, the answer will be no. So, if that doesn't work, well... I only have a few teammates this time. If someone else could take them, then...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: You're not asking me to lead your team, are you?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Look at you, mind reader! So, what do you say? With how strong you are, it would practically be an upgrade for my teammates.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Fine by me, but doesn't that leave you and Kachina as a team of two?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hehe, there's a world of difference between that and flying solo. Besides, we're a formidable duo!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I bet our new friends here will agree that two's always better than one. Right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you mean us?

choices.text: Things are definitely less lonely with Paimon around.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, you're right! Two is definitely better than one!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: It's just like the old saying we have here in Natlan — "No one fights alone."

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: But... what if I drag you down?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Listen to yourself! You'd be hard pressed to find someone in Natlan who can beat us when we're together!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Heh, hearing you say that does make me feel a little more confident...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: *sigh* Still, teams rarely contain more than one Ancient Name bearer. People are definitely gonna think of us as cowards.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: The rules don't forbid it, so who cares what they think!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: It's not like they left us any other option.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Well, I'll leave you to break the news to your soon-to-be former teammates. I'm not good at stuff like that.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Oh, I know.... They deserve to hear it from me, anyway.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Just give me a second, you guys. We can go sign up together once I'm done.

choices.text: It's nice having Paimon by my side.
I'm here to win it.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Oho, a bold statement... I like it, hahaha. The rule against outsider participation is long overdue for a change anyway.

choices.text: This is Paimon. Nice to meet you all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh, and this is {NICKNAME}... Honestly, you could at least introduce yourself a little, you know!

talks.objective: Register for the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: This is the place. Let's wait for Mualani here.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Did you see the flags at the front gate when we entered?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... There were flags, weren't there...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There were all sorts of symbols on them.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Those are our tribal flags — one for each of the six tribes that make up Natlan, including the Children of Echoes.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Why the sudden tour guide routine?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hehe, I said I'd introduce them to Natlan, and we've got nothing better to do, so I might as well deliver on the promise!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Fair enough. Well, I'm from the Scions of the Canopy. We live high in the mountains and have the closest ties to the Yumkasaurs.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: My friend Mualani belongs to the People of the Springs, a seaside tribe. The scenery over there is beautiful, and you can find some really tasty fish.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: That just leaves the Flower-Feather Clan, the Masters of the Night-Wind, and the Collective of Plenty.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: If we get a chance after the Pilgrimage, I'll be sure to show you around.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Well, if we're talking tribes, allow me to stand in for our chief and welcome you on behalf of the People of the Springs.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Mualani, you're back! We were just talking about you!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Everything's settled on my end. My teammates took it unbelievably well, actually. Your reputation is really somethin' else, Kinich.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: They probably just didn't see any drawbacks to your proposition.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We're saying the same thing here. You, my friend, are a formidable competitor, and they recognize that! Anyway, thanks for waiting, you guys. Let's go register.

dialogues.speaker: Cival
dialogues.text: Hello there. Here to register for the Pilgrimage?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's right. I wanted to ask, though... These two travelers are very interested in the competition. Any chance they could take part?

dialogues.speaker: Cival
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but only people from Natlan are eligible to participate.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #You couldn't make an exception just this once? This traveler is a renowned Adventurer! {M#He}{F#She}'s more than skilled enough to participate, and I'm sure the audience would be interested in seeing what {M#he}{F#she} can do.

dialogues.speaker: Cival
dialogues.text: It's not that simple, Miss Mualani. Even a single exception sets a dangerous precedent for countless interested parties in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Cival
dialogues.text: The purpose of the Pilgrimage is not only to select strong warriors, but also to collect Contending Fire from the battles.

dialogues.speaker: Cival
dialogues.text: That is the fire that fuels the Sacred Flame. Natlan is only safe from the invasion of the Abyss while the Sacred Flame burns eternal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so there's another purpose for the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That was the initial purpose, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Every participant, whether they win or lose, contributes to the defense of our nation. That's what makes it such an honor to take part.

dialogues.speaker: Cival
dialogues.text: Exactly right, Mr. Kinich. Contending Fire can only be produced in battles between people of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Cival
dialogues.text: Outlander participation would inhibit the production of this Fire, which could, in turn, jeopardize the Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Ah, so it all comes down to the Contending Fire.

choices.text: It's fine.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Well, you can still enjoy the event from the stands! I'll try to get you some good seats!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That would be great! Tourists like us are better suited to being spectators, anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, there's something Paimon was wondering, actually...

choices.text: If the Ode of Resurrection exists...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You read Paimon's mind, {NICKNAME}! Why doesn't everyone just fight together? Y'know, since you can bring them back to life...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: The power of resurrection has its limits. For starters, the Ode only works on those who bear an Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: That's also why ordinary people who emerge victorious in the Pilgrimage aren't sent to fight the Abyss.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It's for their own protection. Although, they're still afforded the same honor as those who triumph over the Abyss in battle.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: That brings us to the other condition for resurrection. Not much to this one, actually, hahaha. Just one word — "victory"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Victory"?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: "The victors shall burn bright, while the losers must turn to ash."

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Only those who triumph over the Abyss earn the right to be revived. Defeat in battle not only means death, but also the destruction of your Ancient Name, preventing it from ever being inherited again.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: The tales of the vanquished are eventually forgotten, and an Ancient Name cannot survive when the stories of its bearers are lost to time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But, why would the victors need to be revived?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, they won, right? Isn't it the defeated ones who need reviving?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: You have to think about it at the team level. For example, five representatives will be sent to repel the Abyss this time.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Even if four of them were to perish, the Ode of Resurrection would still take effect. All you need is for one person to return victorious.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Because every victory is a building block of our legacy!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Of course, the team needs to be strong enough for that to be the case. Otherwise, the price of failure is still very high.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: That's why the first stage of the Pilgrimage is divided into teams — to instill in us the importance of working together.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: "No one fights alone" — that is what we believe. A lone warrior is one whose defeat is final.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This all sounds pretty dangerous.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Well, that axiom is meant to be a warning as much as a source of inspiration.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Danger is always present, but, together, we can move forward — united in the knowledge that, behind every hero charging into battle, lies the support of all of Natlan as well as our Archon.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Not to mention, the Abyss isn't an enemy with a concrete form. We're often just dealing with the fallout of its scheming.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I've actually fallen in battle myself. I spent some time wandering the realm of the Wayob. It was unlike anything I'd ever experienced before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The realm of the Wayob? Does that mean the Wayob exist somewhere in Natlan?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Hard to say. The realm's not somewhere you can access by ordinary means, and very few people are capable of establishing a mental connection with the Wayob.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: We call this realm the "Night Kingdom," a mysterious, liminal space between the body and mind, life and death.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: The fact that you were resurrected at all is the worst thing in the world.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Then, releasing you from your timeout has gotta come in at a close second.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Hmph, you would do well to speak with reverence of the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw... Lest you live to regret it!

response.speaker: Cival
response.text: If you're done arguing... Your registration is now complete.

response.speaker: Cival
response.text: It all went fairly quickly, considering we all know each other. Now, I just need to register your team members according to their name cards, and you'll be all set.

response.speaker: Cival
response.text: In the meantime, you all can go rest at the hotel. As usual, dinner and lodging for tonight are free.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Nice! Oh yeah, I forgot to mention... All food and entertainment before tomorrow's matches are on the house, courtesy of our Archon!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Family and friends included! Which means, you both get in on it! Come on, let's go have some fun!

choices.text: Why do you have to go through the process of selecting warriors?
I understand the importance of this event.

talks.objective: Go to the Weary Inn for a meal

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Dig in, you guys! Eat as much as you want. These dishes are all local specialties.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: There's more where this came from, too, so don't be shy! Let's feast until the bill gives the Archon a heart attack!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Don't be dramatic...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The Pyro Archon is very generous. Even if it does cause some trouble for all the hotel workers and volunteers...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Speaking of trouble, I've locked Ajaw away for now, so you don't have to worry about him being a nuisance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, isn't that a little harsh?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Eh, Kinich and Ajaw are always like that. Everyone has their own unique way of getting along with their Saurian companion.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: What's got you all down in the dumps, Kachina? You don't have to worry about tomorrow. I'll be with you every step of the way.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I know, I know. Everything's fine, really. I'm just... I'm just nervous.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I can't keep using my age as an excuse. I have to get stronger...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I have to prove to people that I'm not trying to avoid the Night Warden Wars.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You don't have to prove anything to anyone. You know your own heart, so stop beating yourself up over other people's opinions.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: If they don't think you deserve to bear your Ancient Name, they can take it up with the Wayob!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Trust me, Kachina! The Wayob see something special in you!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I just hope it's not the fact that I can take a few punches...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm guessing the Pilgrimage hasn't gone too well in the past?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'm on a seven... or eight-Pilgrimage losing streak. My ranking has been improving little by little, but still, no wins.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: To be honest, losing seven or eight times isn't even a lot. Maybe other people can't see your improvement, but your performance still isn't something to scoff at.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, didn't you say you got really close before?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: It's just... what if I don't even make it through the team stage this time...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hey, have a little faith, will you? You've got me on your team!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Stumble, and I'll be there to get you back on your feet. Run into someone you can't beat, and we'll face them together!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I know you've never tasted victory, but you trust me, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Mualani... *sniff* You're... You're the best!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I trust you, I definitely do! And you're right. I've gotta pull myself together!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I still don't know why the Wayob chose me to inherit an Ancient Name...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: But, I can't be the only bearer who's ever felt this way. If they can keep at it, so can I!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Not to mention... the fact that your Ancient Name has survived until now means all your forebears managed to honor its meaning.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Otherwise, it would be lost to us by now, shattered by defeat in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! And you'll have us rooting for you, too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just call us cheerleaders one and two.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: No, no, no! It should be the other way around. I was clearly the one who asked to learn from you...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: But, still... Thanks, you guys. *sniff* Geez, now I'm crying again... Everyone has been so nice to me today...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I'll win this time, for sure! I won't let your support go to waste!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, right! I should eat something. My mom said I need to keep up my strength for tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice to see your game face back, Kachina!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Thanks for encouraging her, you two. It's easy for people to only see how she still has a lot to learn, so it isn't often that she meets people willing to treat her with patience.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't you worry! We've seen how kind and hard-working she is. We can already tell she's a wonderful person!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: *sniffle*

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Take it easy. You're getting tears in your food.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I—I'll pour you all some drinks. I brought some homemade fruit juice! Lemme just go grab some cups!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She even travels with homemade juice!?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hahaha, Kachina's backpack is practically a bottomless pit. It's got everything.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: *sigh* That's true, but she definitely only offered us some so she could go find somewhere to cry for a little while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like you two really look out for her.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: She's like a little sister to me, you know? She's already so talented, she just needs that one, decisive win to convince her of it.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: And I have a feeling this is the one. This could be the win that finally gives her that confidence!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you so sure? Is that what happened to you?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, no, no. I was just born confident.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Mualani's being modest. She's already a three-time veteran of the Night Warden Wars. Came out on top each time — and she's never had to be resurrected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Eh, it's no big deal. The opponents I had to face were pretty tame, that's all... No, wait, that makes it sound too unimpressive...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Either way, the challenges haven't been that difficult so far. But, I'd love to fight alongside Kachina and experience the glory of victory together — the flowers, the applause...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon gets it! That's how Paimon and {NICKNAME} are too!

choices.text: Fighting side by side? Yeah, I guess...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! A little more confidence, please! Paimon's always there to cheer you on!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Drinks are here! Better try them while they're still fresh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Feeling better now, Kachina?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Me? Hehe, I'm totally fine! Really, I promise. That was just nerves, earlier.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I'm gonna get some meat in my system, then head out to get some exercise. Wanna be nice and loose for the tournament tomorrow.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I'll come with you!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Just don't go overboard, okay? The last thing we need is for someone to oversleep. We've got an early day tomorrow.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hehe, if only we had a friend who never oversleeps...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: ...Alright, fine. I'll make sure you guys are up on time.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Attaboy! I knew you'd catch on!

choices.text: Fighting side by side? Are we, really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Of course! Just think about it, {NICKNAME}. Where would you be without your guide?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The statue is so pretty! Is that what the Pyro Archon is like?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: You betcha! Beautiful, effortlessly confident, and absolutely awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: E—Eh!? Wait, wait, wait... You can use it too? How?

choices.text: It just came naturally.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: That... was... AMAZING! I don't even know what to say!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, look behind you! Something's coming!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do we do? Is something after us? Should we get ready to fight!?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: We're fine, we're fine! This, here, is Toto!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Hiya, Toto! Hehe, it's me, Kachina!

response.speaker: Toto
response.text: Roar...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Well, aren't we looking lively today? Did the Chiselith lure you over here? Warm, isn't it?

response.speaker: Toto
response.text: Roar...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so it was just a friendly Saurian... Wait, is that a Saurian?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Nope, that's a Long-Necked Rhino. There's quite a few of them around here, and Toto's the friendliest and gentlest of the bunch.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: He's always hanging around these parts. I swear he does it just to show off to any outlanders that might come this way. Don't let his size fool you, though. He's just a big softie!

response.speaker: Toto
response.text: Roar—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, what does the crouching mean?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: That's an invitation. He's offering us a ride!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't mind if we do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon's not so sure about this. It's kinda scary, don't you think? He's huge!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are you scared of? You can fly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, good point! You guys have fun with that, then. Paimon will just float alongside!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! The sightseeing is even better from up here!

choices.text: All in a day's work.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: One picture to publish, and one to keep for myself. Perfect!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I heard there's a place in Natlan that produces precious stones. Next time there's a lull in my work, I gotta go pay it a visit.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: #Safe travels, {NICKNAME}. You're welcome back anytime. If you let us know in advance, we could arrange even more people to greet you when you return.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: That would be quite the lively affair.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Ayo! Come on, over here!

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce you! This is Ayo, my Saurian companion, and also an important member of my family.

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar~ ♪

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hehe, he's saying hello! I think he likes you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Saurian"... So, in Natlan, you consider Saurians to be part of your family?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Of course! Natlan is not only a nation of heroes, but also a nation of Saurians. They occupy an important place in every tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Outlanders always seem to think of Ayo as my pet, but that's not the case at all.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Ayo and I go on adventures together, but he also has a Saurian family and a place to stay of his own. Sometimes, he even brings his entire family over to eat at our house.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The Children of Echoes have the closest ties to the Tepetlisaurs, which are naturally very friendly to humans. That's how our relationship became what it is today.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: All Saurians have their own personalities, but... I think calling them our "companions" pretty much sums it up!

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: See? Ayo agrees with me!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: #Safe travels, {NICKNAME}. You're welcome back anytime. If you let us know in advance, we could arrange even more people to greet you when you return.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back! Did you forget something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Huh...? That's not right. Is the Statue asleep, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...I don't sense anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, shouldn't you be able to shoot fireballs or summon flame pillars by now?

choices.text: Nothing happened...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Strange... Must be something unique to Natlan.

choices.text: I don't sense any elemental energy either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It didn't work when you tried earlier, either. Now we know that wasn't a fluke... What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh? You can get elemental power from the Statue of The Seven?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's always worked before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This would've been such a good opportunity to show Kachina how impressive you are...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's so weird that it's not working... There must be something about Natlan...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Aw, I would've liked to see that...

dialogues.speaker: Cival
dialogues.text: Get a good rest, everyone. I wish you all the best in tomorrow's competition.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, check out those colorful pictures on the walls!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've gotta be on the right track!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that thing over there looks super intimidating. You sure it's not gonna fall off?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hahaha, don't worry! Our tribe works closely with stone. That's one of our symbols, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: It's not going anywhere, I promise you!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Many of our tribespeople love music and dance, and have an amazing sense of rhythm.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: In the past, outlanders have come here just to study our culture and exchange views.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: My parents wanted me to learn dance, but I wanted to become a warrior instead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So full... *yawn* and so sleepy... We should get a good night's sleep before the competition tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's still a little worried about Kachina, though. Maybe we can help her out with her training?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She did say she wanted to learn from us... Not that Paimon's gonna be doing much of the teaching...
